headline: Agent-based and non-Markovian models link network topology to epidemic outcomes
label: Agent Based Epidemic Network Modeling
summary: Recent preprints and a published Julia tool extend agent-based epidemic modeling to evolving networks and non-Markovian disease dynamics.
synthesis: The common thread is population-level behavior emerging from explicitly specified individual-level rules on networks or agent populations. A non-Markovian SIR study derives outbreak-size distributions on complex networks by mapping the process to an effective Markovian process with a single edge-level description. A coevolution study models a fatal disease with waning immunity on a scale-free network that evolves over time, reporting an epidemic transition and loss of power-law degree structure. AgentBasedModeling.jl offers a Julia implementation of stochastic continuous-time agent-based simulation linking intracellular reaction networks to population dynamics. The items differ in biological focus and do not share a single system. What is new is the explicit coupling of network topology, state-dependent disease processes, and simulation tooling within one framework.
